TITLE: Apple Mail
DESC: Apple Mail CLI for AI agents: list, search and read mail; policy-gated triage (mark, move, trash). Never sends mail.
SCOPE_HELP: mailbox paths `Account/Mailbox/Sub` (local: `On My Mac/Name`) and, for drafts, `draft:<sender address>` or `draft:default`
INJECTION: Static JXA script (`go:embed`). Input travels only as one JSON argv element to `/usr/bin/osascript` (absolute path), and fuzz tests check the script and argv shape are invariant. Message bodies are parsed in Go (MIME, HTML to text), never in Mail.
SECRETS: No credentials are involved, and the CLI has no send, reply or forward command; `draft` only saves drafts. Attachment contents are never read.
ONELINER: Read, search, triage and draft Apple Mail from the command line, built for AI coding agents. It cannot send mail.
PERMISSION_HINT: macOS has not allowed the app that runs the CLI to control Mail
INTEGRATION_NOTE: Mail cannot delete mailboxes through scripting, so the Mail tests reuse one local mailbox, `On My Mac/agent-cli-test-sandbox`, which they create on the first run. They read real messages but never change them; writes against real messages are only used to check that the policy blocks them.
AGENT_TASK: reading, triaging and drafting the user's email (it cannot send mail)
FIRST_RUN: On the first run macOS asks whether your terminal app may control Mail.
NETWORK_SECTION: `apple-mail` makes no network connections of its own. It asks Mail for data, and Mail syncs with your accounts as usual.
DEFAULT_ACCESS: `apple-mail` reads mail and saves drafts out of the box. Everything else, and switching drafts off, is set in
DEFAULT_NOTE: The one exception is `draft`: saving a draft is on by default, because nothing leaves the machine until a person sends it from Mail. `"operations": {"deny": ["draft"]}` turns it off.
